translationRepairs: He was made Commander-in-Chief and garrisoned Zhengzhou.
He was made Commander-in-Chief and garrisoned Shanzhou.
s0068 has 鎮鄯州; 鄯州 is Shanzhou, not Zhengzhou (鄭州), and the following Huanghe posting fits the western corridor.
He was made Commander-in-Chief and garrisoned Zhengzhou.
He was made Commander-in-Chief and garrisoned Shanzhou.
Same unit reads 鎮鄯州; the literal must match Shanzhou rather than Zhengzhou.
From the time Gui garrisoned Zhengzhou, he defeated them in battle after battle.
From the time Gui garrisoned Shanzhou, he defeated them in battle after battle.
s0076 has 自檜鎮鄯州; the place is again Shanzhou, and replacing Zhengzhou corrects a clear naming error without other changes.
From the time Gui garrisoned Zhengzhou, in battle after battle he was sure to defeat them.
From the time Gui garrisoned Shanzhou, in battle after battle he was sure to defeat them.
Literal of s0076 likewise mistranslates 鄯州 as Zhengzhou; Shanzhou is the accurate reading.
Before long the Grand Progenitor said to Gui, "You formerly at Zhengzhou showed loyalty and courage in full measure.
Before long the Grand Progenitor said to Gui, "You formerly at Shanzhou showed loyalty and courage in full measure.
s0086 quotes 卿昔在鄯州; the speech refers to Shanzhou, and Shanzhou fits the following remark that the western border is cleared.
Before long the Grand Progenitor said to Gui, "You formerly at Zhengzhou showed loyalty and courage in full.
Before long the Grand Progenitor said to Gui, "You formerly at Shanzhou showed loyalty and courage in full.
Literal of s0086 has the same 在鄯州; Zhengzhou is wrong and Shanzhou is correct.
Earlier, Zhongmi had fallen out with Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel.
Earlier, Zhongmi had fallen out with Cui Xian of the Ministry of Personnel.
s0035 names 崔暹; 暹 is Xian, not Xuan (宣), so Cui Xian is the correct English form.
Earlier, Zhongmi had a rift with Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel.
Earlier, Zhongmi had a rift with Cui Xian of the Ministry of Personnel.
Literal of s0035 likewise must render 崔暹 as Cui Xian rather than Cui Xuan.
Xuan was then entrusted with authority by Prince Wenxiang of Qi, and Zhongmi feared he would plot against him; uneasy at every turn, he planned to defect and surrender.
Xian was then entrusted with authority by Prince Wenxiang of Qi, and Zhongmi feared he would plot against him; uneasy at every turn, he planned to defect and surrender.
s0036 opens with 暹 referring to the same 崔暹; the subject should be Xian, not Xuan.
